summary: Completed the evidence-backed review of Tesla, Inc. common stock after the 2026-07-28 RSI-oversold transition. The immutable TSLA/XNAS/USD identity is unique and now linked to a maintained security page. The shares fell 25.49% over the measured month and RSI reached 26.93, while the close remained just above the lower Bollinger band. Tesla's Q2 filing is temporally aligned with the largest repricing: revenue rose 26% and deliveries reached 480,126, but operating income fell 57%, capital expenditures nearly doubled, and the shares fell 14.52% in the first post-results session on unusually high volume. Strong liquidity supports medium-confidence baseline comparison, but a bounded revenue-multiple range gives 44.8% downside and a base value 13.6% below the USD 306.86 mark. No conviction strategy or idea refresh was queued because the full strategy gate failed and neither the payload nor an accepted canonical relationship names an idea.

evidence.claim: Tesla's Q2 2026 Form 10-Q confirms TSLA common stock on Nasdaq and reports quarterly revenue of USD 28.236 billion, up 26% year over year, gross profit of USD 4.751 billion, operating income of USD 398 million, down 57%, and common-stockholder net income of USD 1.114 billion. At June 30, cash and short-term investments were USD 43.524 billion against USD 9.08 billion of debt principal; six-month operating cash flow was USD 8.634 billion and capital expenditures were USD 8.282 billion. Management expects more than USD 25 billion of 2026 capital expenditures, primarily for AI, manufacturing, research, fleet, and supporting infrastructure.

Tesla's issuer release reports Q2 2026 production of 451,758 vehicles, deliveries of 480,126 vehicles, and energy-storage deployments of 13.5 GWh. The issuer cautions that these measures alone do not determine financial performance because pricing, costs, foreign exchange, and other factors also matter.
